schema.description: The page number of paginated results.
The number of WAF overrides per page.

description.description: An informative summary of the current URI-based WAF override.
description.example: Enable Cloudflare Magento ruleset for shop.example.com

groups.description: An object that allows you to enable or disable WAF rule groups for the current WAF override. Each key of this object must be the ID of a WAF rule group, and each value must be a valid WAF action (usually `default` or `disable`). When creating a new URI-based WAF override, you must provide a `groups` object or a `rules` object.

id.description: The unique identifier of the WAF override.

paused.description: When true, indicates that the rule is currently paused.

priority.description: The relative priority of the current URI-based WAF override when multiple overrides match a single URL. A lower number indicates higher priority. Higher priority overrides may overwrite values set by lower priority overrides.

rewrite_action.description: Specifies that, when a WAF rule matches, its configured action will be replaced by the action configured in this object.

block.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

challenge.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

default.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

disable.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

simulate.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

rules.description: An object that allows you to override the action of specific WAF rules. Each key of this object must be the ID of a WAF rule, and each value must be a valid WAF action. Unless you are disabling a rule, ensure that you also enable the rule group that this WAF rule belongs to. When creating a new URI-based WAF override, you must provide a `groups` object or a `rules` object.

allOf.description: The WAF rule action to apply.

urls.description: The URLs to include in the current WAF override. You can use wildcards. Each entered URL will be escaped before use, which means you can only use simple wildcard patterns.
